title: Grateful Dead Live at Cafe au Go-Go on 1969-09-29
lineage: AUD > ? > Reel > Cass (Maxell UD w/dolby B, playback on SonyTCK-909ES) > DAT (SV-3700 w/Oade +15dB input gain mod) > ZA2 > DiamondCutNoise Reduction > CD

ai_review.summary: Muddy, cassette‑sourced audience tape, but it captures the historic “The Seven” jam that makes this show a must‑listen.
ai_review.review: This recording is an audience AUD capture on a Maxell UD cassette, so the mix is muddy, vocals are often lost and the high‑frequency range is harsh.  Despite those flaws the performance shines – the rare seven‑minute “The Seven” jam (sandwiched between Doin’ That Rag and Good Lovin’) is repeatedly praised as mind‑blowing, with standout guitar work from both Jerry and Bob, solid bass from Phil, and fire‑cracker drumming by Bill and Mickey.  Overall fans recommend it for the music rather than the sound quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating is 4.28 across 18 reviews; most reviewers love the performance (especially The Seven) while repeatedly noting poor audio quality, yielding a strong but balanced overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape recorded on Maxell UD cassette; vocals ~90% missing, muddy mids, bright highs from Dolby B, occasional drop‑outs. Mix is surprisingly balanced for an audience source but lacks clarity and EQ.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show builds from a solid first set into an unexpected jam sequence – Doin' That Rag segues straight into the legendary Seven and then into Good Lovin', followed by a tight St. Stephen > The Eleven transition that keeps the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s leads are described as manic, snakey and dazzling throughout the jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is noted as audible and supportive, holding down the groove during the complex sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s rhythm/lead guitar shines in the mix; several reviewers highlight his shimmering tone on The Seven.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ is described as buried in tape hiss and not cutting through well.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart receive high praise for tight, war‑speed synchronization and powerful drumming.
